w10_T4_002025: Ines had 103 bags of cement stacked at the yard. She used 37 bags on the garage floor. Her partner Bruno, who had far fewer bags of his own, took 30 from her stack for the patio. A merchant then delivered 22 bags to Ines. Another 30 went into the driveway. Every bag still in Ines's stack fills 8 buckets of mix, and the yard bills its deliveries in minutes rather than hours. How many buckets of mix could Ines's remaining cement fill?
w10_T4_002028: Ola counted 240 boxes in the depot, and her colleague Piet, who manages a smaller depot, sent over 28 more of the same size. Every box holds 6 sleeves. Each sleeve contains 9 wallets, and a courier added 26 loose wallets to the shelves. Every wallet holds 6 cards, and a late delivery brought 26 loose cards as well. The depot has a dozen loading doors and stands 400 metres from the motorway. How many cards are in the depot?
w10_T4_002034: Nadia brought 199 apples in from the orchard, and her brother Emil, who picked fewer than she did, added 32 from his own basket. The kitchen used 54 apples for a crumble that afternoon. The rest were shared equally between 3 market boxes, and Nadia took the first box to the stall. She sold 17 apples from that box before the rain started. The orchard has 64 trees. How many apples are left in Nadia's box?
w10_T4_002036: In the morning a print room had 184 reams of paper and used 136 of them on a school order. Every ream still on the shelf was split into 2 half-packs for easier carrying. Each half-pack was found to hold 5 blocks, and every block contains 8 sheets. During the afternoon and evening 199 sheets were spoiled by a faulty printer. The print room is 12 metres square. How many sheets are left?
w10_T4_002037: A hire company had 131 folding tables in its warehouse. An inspection scrapped 7 of them with broken hinges. A customer failed to return 8 more after a wedding. A closing hotel then sold the company 34 tables, and a manufacturer delivered 35 new ones. A festival hired 51 tables for the whole summer and took them away. The warehouse also stores 900 chairs. How many tables are in the warehouse now?
w10_T4_002039: On Monday morning Ramona baked 57 trays of biscuits, and each tray held 5 rows. Every row was made up of 3 biscuits. In the afternoon her partner Ken, who baked fewer trays than Ramona, packed all the biscuits equally into 3 hampers and set the first hamper aside for the school. In the evening 42 biscuits were eaten from that hamper at a tasting. The bakery van holds 26 hampers. How many biscuits are left in the first hamper?
w10_T4_002041: On Saturday morning Tia had 27 tubs of paint in the shed and used 26 of them on the mural. The tub still unopened fills 9 small jars. In the afternoon she shared those jars equally between 3 art tables. In the evening her friend Ola set out 3 tables so that each one matched Tia's first table exactly, jar for jar, though Ola had started the day with far fewer jars than Tia. How many jars did Ola set out on those 3 tables altogether?
w10_T4_002048: In the morning a market gardener cut 26 bunches of daffodils and a helper cut 12 more. Every bunch holds 5 stems. Each stem carries 3 buds. In the afternoon a grower delivered 63 loose buds for the same display. In the evening 236 buds were sold to a hotel. The delivery van had covered 87 kilometres that day. How many buds are left?
w10_T4_002049: Early in the morning a warehouse counted 113 pallets, and each pallet carried 3 crates. Every crate holds 8 tins. At midday the tins were shared equally between 6 shops, and the High Street shop took the first share. During the afternoon a supplier added 61 tins to that shop's stock, and 478 tins were sold from it. In the evening a returned order brought 19 tins back to the same shelf. The shop has a dozen staff and a car park with 30 spaces. How many tins does the High Street shop have?
w10_T4_002059: A school had 81 packets of seeds and used 77 of them on the vegetable beds. Every packet still in the drawer holds 7 seeds. A parent donated 62 loose seeds to go with them. The seeds were then shared equally between 2 classes, and Class Willow received the first share. The school has a dozen raised beds and a greenhouse 5 metres long. How many seeds did Class Willow receive?
w10_T4_002061: A cafe opened the morning with 22 loaves on the rack and sold 11 of them before nine. A delivery at ten added 50 more loaves. Around midday the kitchen baked another 35, and in the early afternoon a partner bakery sent 23 across. Through the rest of the afternoon and the evening 102 loaves were sold. The cafe has been open for a dozen years and writes its baking times in minutes rather than hours. How many loaves are left on the rack?
w10_T4_002062: In the morning Dmitri stacked 230 boxes onto each of 5 lorries. Every box holds 4 packets of rice. During the afternoon all of the packets were shared equally between 5 depots, and Dmitri's own depot took the first share. His colleague Petra, whose depot received exactly as much as the others, sent him 42 spare packets from her store that evening. A late van added another 43 packets to Dmitri's depot. How many packets does Dmitri's depot hold?
w10_T4_002064: A bookshop opened the morning with 201 boxes in the stockroom and took in 80 more before lunch. In the early afternoon 25 boxes were sent to the branch across town. Later that afternoon a returned order brought 17 boxes back to the stockroom. In the evening the staff counted the boxes and confirmed that every one of them holds 8 paperbacks. How many paperbacks are in the stockroom?
w10_T4_002065: A cider farm had 112 sacks of apples and picked 50 more from the top field. Every sack holds 4 kilograms of fruit. A neighbour added 62 kilograms of loose apples to the barn. The whole load was then split equally between 2 presses, and the old press took the first share. Pressing lost 125 kilograms as pulp at the old press. The farm covers 30 hectares and has been in the family for a dozen generations. How many kilograms remain at the old press?
w10_T4_002066: A hospital linen store held 215 pillowcases. An inspection removed 13 that were badly stained. Another 30 went to the day ward, and 88 more were sent up to the new wing. A laundry return then added 75 clean pillowcases to the store. Another 28 went out to the maternity unit. The same team has run this store for a dozen years, and its laundry rota is written in minutes rather than hours. How many pillowcases are in the store now?
w10_T4_002070: A theatre had 157 costumes in its wardrobe room. A closing company donated 20 more. A local college added 69 costumes from its old store. The touring production then took 136 costumes away with it. A repair shop returned 23 costumes it had been mending. The theatre itself seats 420 people. How many costumes are in the wardrobe room now?
w10_T4_002073: In the morning a bakery had 74 bags of flour and the mill delivered 29 more. By the afternoon a bulk order had raised the store to 2 times that number of bags. Later that afternoon the bags were shared equally between 2 kitchens, and the front kitchen took the first share. In the evening a supplier added 10 bags to the front kitchen, and a returned order brought 51 more. The bakery pays 60 pounds a week for deliveries and records its proving times in minutes rather than hours. How many bags of flour are in the front kitchen?
w10_T4_002076: Early in the morning a farm shop had 205 trays of eggs and a delivery brought 49 more. Every tray in the shop holds 6 eggs. Before lunch 752 eggs were sold to a hotel, and during the afternoon a bakery bought another 165. In the evening the shop worked out that each egg still in stock would sell for 8 pence. A customer then dropped 79 pence into the same till as a tip. The shop has kept hens for a dozen years. How many pence does the till hold from those eggs?
w10_T4_002080: A charity shop had 159 books on its shelves in January, and by March its book stock had doubled. A house clearance added 76 more books to the same shelves. Customers then bought 289 books over the spring. A school donated 41 books in April. A car boot sale took another 85 books away from the shop. How many books are on the shelves now?
w10_T4_002081: A club printed 25 sheets of raffle tickets, and each sheet carried 9 tickets. A second printing doubled the number of tickets the club held. A member then brought in 43 tickets left over from last year, and the treasurer found 9 more in a drawer. Before the draw the printer ran off enough extras to double the club's ticket count once again. The club records its meeting lengths in minutes rather than hours. How many tickets does the club have now?
w10_T4_002087: Ahmed loaded 96 crates onto each of 3 lorries. Every crate holds 9 melons. His partner Sara, who loaded fewer crates than Ahmed did, sold 1019 melons at the wholesale market. A supermarket then bought 1543 melons from the same load. The farm covers 55 hectares and has grown melons for a dozen years. How many melons are left?
w10_T4_002088: A joinery had 181 lengths of timber and sent 42 of them back as warped. A merchant delivered 14 more lengths that week, and a cancelled job returned 80 to the rack. Every length on the rack can be cut into 4 shelf boards. Fitting out a library then used 655 of those boards. The workshop is 18 metres long and quotes its jobs in minutes rather than hours. How many shelf boards are left?
w10_T4_002089: A gym had 125 towels in the reception cupboard and threw out 7 that were fraying. A delivery added 69 fresh towels the same afternoon. Over the next month the gym's towel stock grew to 2 times that number. A member then donated 8 towels she no longer needed. The gym has 240 members on its books. How many towels does the gym have now?
w10_T4_002090: On Monday morning a wholesaler split 78 sacks of onions equally between 3 shops. Before lunch a grower delivered 70 more sacks to the first shop. Every sack in that shop holds 5 kilograms of onions. In the afternoon Mira added 35 kilograms of loose onions from her own crate, rather more than her colleague Josef had brought in. Later that afternoon a restaurant bought 164 kilograms from the shop. Through the evening a market trader took another 333 kilograms away. The shop has traded here for a dozen years. How many kilograms of onions are left in the first shop?
w10_T4_002092: Lena had 49 sheets of stamps in her album and bought 28 more at the fair. She swapped 23 sheets away for a poster. The rest she divided equally between 2 folders, keeping the red folder for herself. Her cousin Tobias, who owns fewer stamps than Lena, gave her 70 sheets for the red folder. A dealer sold her another 34 sheets for the same folder. Lena's catalogue prices everything in cents rather than dollars. How many sheets are in the red folder?
